NASB.1: And all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who [was] sixteen years old, and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.
NASB.2: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah after the king slept with his fathers.
NASB.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jechiliah of Jerusalem.
NASB.4: He did right in the sight of the LORD according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
NASB.5: He continued to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding through the vision of God; and as long as he sought the LORD, God prospered him.
NASB.6: Now he went out and warred against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath and the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in [the area of] Ashdod and among the Philistines.
NASB.7: God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.
NASB.8: The Ammonites also gave tribute to Uzziah, and his fame extended to the border of Egypt, for he became very strong.
NASB.9: Moreover, Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate and at the Valley Gate and at the corner buttress and fortified them.
NASB.10: He built towers in the wilderness and hewed many cisterns, for he had much livestock, both in the lowland and in the plain. [He also had] plowmen and vinedressers in the hill country and the fertile fields, for he loved the soil.
NASB.11: Moreover, Uzziah had an army ready for battle, which entered combat by divisions according to the number of their muster, prepared by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the official, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's officers.
NASB.12: The total number of the heads of the households, of valiant warriors, was 2,600.
NASB.13: Under their direction was an elite army of 307,500, who could wage war with great power, to help the king against the enemy.
NASB.14: Moreover, Uzziah prepared for all the army shields, spears, helmets, body armor, bows and sling stones.
NASB.15: In Jerusalem he made engines [of war] invented by skillful men to be on the towers and on the corners for the purpose of shooting arrows and great stones. Hence his fame spread afar, for he was marvelously helped until he [was] strong.
NASB.16: But when he became strong, his heart was so proud that he acted corruptly, and he was unfaithful to the LORD his God, for he entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
NASB.17: Then Azariah the priest entered after him and with him eighty priests of the LORD, valiant men.
NASB.18: They opposed Uzziah the king and said to him, 'It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron who are consecrated to burn incense. Get out of the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful and will have no honor from the LORD God.'
NASB.19: But Uzziah, with a censer in his hand for burning incense, was enraged; and while he was enraged with the priests, the leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.
NASB.20: Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, and behold, he [was] leprous on his forehead; and they hurried him out of there, and he himself also hastened to get out because the LORD had smitten him.
NASB.21: King Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death; and he lived in a separate house, being a leper, for he was cut off from the house of the LORD. And Jotham his son [was] over the king's house judging the people of the land.
NASB.22: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first to last, the prophet Isaiah, the son of Amoz, has written.
NASB.23: So Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the grave which belonged to the kings, for they said, 'He is a leper.' And Jotham his son became king in his place.

NKJV.1: Now all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king instead of his father Amaziah.
NKJV.2: He built Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king rested with his fathers.
NKJV.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.
NKJV.4: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
NKJV.5: He sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God; and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.
NKJV.6: Now he went out and made war against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities around Ashdod and among the Philistines.
NKJV.7: God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabians who lived in Gur Baal, and against the Meunites.
NKJV.8: Also the Ammonites brought tribute to Uzziah. His fame spread as far as the entrance of Egypt, for he became exceedingly strong.
NKJV.9: And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the corner buttress of the wall; then he fortified them.
NKJV.10: Also he built towers in the desert. He dug many wells, for he had much livestock, both in the lowlands and in the plains; he also had farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in Carmel, for he loved the soil.
NKJV.11: Moreover Uzziah had an army of fighting men who went out to war by companies, according to the number on their roll as prepared by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king’s captains.
NKJV.12: The total number of chief officers of the mighty men of valor was two thousand six hundred.
NKJV.13: And under their authority was an army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, that made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
NKJV.14: Then Uzziah prepared for them, for the entire army, shields, spears, helmets, body armor, bows, and slings to cast stones.
NKJV.15: And he made devices in Jerusalem, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and large stones. So his fame spread far and wide, for he was marvelously helped till he became strong.
NKJV.16: But when he was strong his heart was lifted up, to his destruction, for he transgressed against the LORD his God by entering the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
NKJV.17: So Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him were eighty priests of the LORD—valiant men.
NKJV.18: And they withstood King Uzziah, and said to him, “It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Get out of the sanctuary, for you have trespassed! You shall have no honor from the LORD God.”
NKJV.19: Then Uzziah became furious; and he had a censer in his hand to burn incense. And while he was angry with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead, before the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the incense altar.
NKJV.20: And Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, and there, on his forehead, he was leprous; so they thrust him out of that place. Indeed he also hurried to get out, because the LORD had struck him.
NKJV.21: King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death. He dwelt in an isolated house, because he was a leper; for he was cut off from the house of the LORD. Then Jotham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.
NKJV.22: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz wrote.
NKJV.23: So Uzziah rested with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of burial which belonged to the kings, for they said, “He is a leper.” Then Jotham his son reigned in his place.

ESV.1: And all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king instead of his father Amaziah.
ESV.2: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah, after the king slept with his fathers.
ESV.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
ESV.4: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
ESV.5: He set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who instructed him in the fear of God, and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.
ESV.6: He went out and made war against the Philistines and broke through the wall of Gath and the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod, and he built cities in the territory of Ashdod and elsewhere among the Philistines.
ESV.7: God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabians who lived in Gurbaal and against the Meunites.
ESV.8: The Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread even to the border of Egypt, for he became very strong.
ESV.9: Moreover, Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate and at the Valley Gate and at the Angle, and fortified them.
ESV.10: And he built towers in the wilderness and cut out many cisterns, for he had large herds, both in the Shephelah and in the plain, and he had farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fertile lands, for he loved the soil.
ESV.11: Moreover, Uzziah had an army of soldiers, fit for war, in divisions according to the numbers in the muster made by Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the officer, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
ESV.12: The whole number of the heads of fathers' houses of mighty men of valor was 2,600.
ESV.13: Under their command was an army of 307,500, who could make war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
ESV.14: And Uzziah prepared for all the army shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slinging.
ESV.15: In Jerusalem he made machines, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and great stones. And his fame spread far, for he was marvelously helped, till he was strong.
ESV.16: But when he was strong, he grew proud, to his destruction. For he was unfaithful to the LORD his God and entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
ESV.17: But Azariah the priest went in after him, with eighty priests of the LORD who were men of valor,
ESV.18: and they withstood King Uzziah and said to him, “It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have done wrong, and it will bring you no honor from the LORD God.”
ESV.19: Then Uzziah was angry. Now he had a censer in his hand to burn incense, and when he became angry with the priests, leprosy  broke out on his forehead in the presence of the priests in the house of the LORD, by the altar of incense.
ESV.20: And Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, and behold, he was leprous in his forehead! And they rushed him out quickly, and he himself hurried to go out, because the LORD had struck him.
ESV.21: And King Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death, and being a leper lived in a separate house, for he was excluded from the house of the LORD. And Jotham his son was over the king's household, governing the people of the land.
ESV.22: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz wrote.
ESV.23: And Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, “He is a leper.” And Jotham his son reigned in his place.

WEB.1: All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.
WEB.2: He built Eloth, and restored it to Judah, after that the king slept with his fathers.
WEB.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign; and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jechiliah, of Jerusalem.
WEB.4: He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
WEB.5: He set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the vision of God; and as long as he sought Yahweh, God made him prosper.
WEB.6: He went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in the country of Ashdod, and among the Philistines.
WEB.7: God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians who lived in Gur Baal, and the Meunim.
WEB.8: The Ammonites gave tribute to Uzziah. His name spread abroad even to the entrance of Egypt; for he grew exceedingly strong.
WEB.9: Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, at the valley gate, and at the turning of the wall, and fortified them.
WEB.10: He built towers in the wilderness, and dug out many cisterns, for he had much livestock; in the lowland also, and in the plain. He had farmers and vineyard keepers in the mountains and in the fruitful fields, for he loved farming.
WEB.11: Moreover Uzziah had an army of fighting men, who went out to war by bands, according to the number of their reckoning made by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king’s captains.
WEB.12: The whole number of the heads of fathers’ households, even the mighty men of valor, was two thousand six hundred.
WEB.13: Under their hand was an army, three hundred seven thousand five hundred, who made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
WEB.14: Uzziah prepared for them, even for all the army, shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slinging.
WEB.15: In Jerusalem, he made devices, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and on the battlements, with which to shoot arrows and great stones. His name spread far abroad, because he was marvelously helped until he was strong.
WEB.16: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up, so that he did corruptly, and he trespassed against Yahweh his God; for he went into Yahweh’s temple to burn incense on the altar of incense.
WEB.17: Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of Yahweh, who were valiant men.

WEB.19: Then Uzziah was angry. He had a censer in his hand to burn incense, and while he was angry with the priests, the leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in Yahweh’s house, beside the altar of incense.
WEB.20: Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked at him, and behold, he was leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out quickly from there. Yes, he himself also hurried to go out, because Yahweh had struck him.
WEB.21: Uzziah the king was a leper to the day of his death, and lived in a separate house, being a leper; for he was cut off from Yahweh’s house. Jotham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.
WEB.22: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, wrote.
WEB.23: So Uzziah slept with his fathers; and they buried him with his fathers in the field of burial which belonged to the kings, for they said, “He is a leper.” Jotham his son reigned in his place.

NLT.1: All the people of Judah had crowned Amaziah’s sixteen-year-old son, Uzziah, as king in place of his father.
NLT.2: After his father’s death, Uzziah rebuilt the town of Elath and restored it to Judah.
NLT.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. His mother was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
NLT.4: He did what was pleasing in the LORD’s sight, just as his father, Amaziah, had done.
NLT.5: Uzziah sought God during the days of Zechariah, who taught him to fear God. And as long as the king sought guidance from the LORD, God gave him success.
NLT.6: Uzziah declared war on the Philistines and broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod. Then he built new towns in the Ashdod area and in other parts of Philistia.
NLT.7: God helped him in his wars against the Philistines, his battles with the Arabs of Gur, and his wars with the Meunites.
NLT.8: The Meunites paid annual tribute to him, and his fame spread even to Egypt, for he had become very powerful.
NLT.9: Uzziah built fortified towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the angle in the wall.
NLT.10: He also constructed forts in the wilderness and dug many water cisterns, because he kept great herds of livestock in the foothills of Judah and on the plains. He was also a man who loved the soil. He had many workers who cared for his farms and vineyards, both on the hillsides and in the fertile valleys.
NLT.11: Uzziah had an army of well-trained warriors, ready to march into battle, unit by unit. This army had been mustered and organized by Jeiel, the secretary of the army, and his assistant, Maaseiah. They were under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king’s officials.
NLT.12: These regiments of mighty warriors were commanded by 2,600 clan leaders.
NLT.13: The army consisted of 307,500 men, all elite troops. They were prepared to assist the king against any enemy.
NLT.14: Uzziah provided the entire army with shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and sling stones.
NLT.15: And he built structures on the walls of Jerusalem, designed by experts to protect those who shot arrows and hurled large stones from the towers and the corners of the wall. His fame spread far and wide, for the LORD gave him marvelous help, and he became very powerful.
NLT.16: But when he had become powerful, he also became proud, which led to his downfall. He sinned against the LORD his God by entering the sanctuary of the LORD’s Temple and personally burning incense on the incense altar.
NLT.17: Azariah the high priest went in after him with eighty other priests of the LORD, all brave men.
NLT.18: They confronted King Uzziah and said, “It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD. That is the work of the priests alone, the descendants of Aaron who are set apart for this work. Get out of the sanctuary, for you have sinned. The LORD God will not honor you for this!”
NLT.19: Uzziah, who was holding an incense burner, became furious. But as he was standing there raging at the priests before the incense altar in the LORD’s Temple, leprosy suddenly broke out on his forehead.
NLT.20: When Azariah the high priest and all the other priests saw the leprosy, they rushed him out. And the king himself was eager to get out because the LORD had struck him.
NLT.21: So King Uzziah had leprosy until the day he died. He lived in isolation in a separate house, for he was excluded from the Temple of the LORD. His son Jotham was put in charge of the royal palace, and he governed the people of the land.
NLT.22: The rest of the events of Uzziah’s reign, from beginning to end, are recorded by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
NLT.23: When Uzziah died, he was buried with his ancestors; his grave was in a nearby burial field belonging to the kings, for the people said, “He had leprosy.” And his son Jotham became the next king.

CSB17.1: All the people <sup>ⓙ</sup> of Judah took Uzziah, <sup>[1]</sup> who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
CSB17.2: After Amaziah the king rested with his fathers, Uzziah rebuilt Eloth <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓚ</sup> and restored it to Judah.
CSB17.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old <sup>ⓛ</sup> when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem.
CSB17.4: He did what was right in the LORD’s sight just as his father Amaziah had done.
CSB17.5: He sought God <sup>ⓜ</sup> throughout the lifetime of Zechariah, the teacher of the fear <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓝ</sup> of God. During the time that he sought the LORD, God gave him success. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.6: Uzziah went out to wage war against the Philistines, <sup>ⓑ</sup> and he tore down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod. Then he built cities in the vicinity of Ashdod and among the Philistines.
CSB17.7: God helped him against the Philistines, the Arabs that live in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.
CSB17.8: The Ammonites <sup>[4]</sup> paid tribute to Uzziah, <sup>ⓒ</sup> and his fame spread as far as the entrance of Egypt, for God made him very powerful.
CSB17.9: Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, <sup>ⓓ</sup> the Valley Gate, <sup>ⓔ</sup> and the corner buttress, and he fortified them.
CSB17.10: Since he had many cattle both in the Judean foothills <sup>[5]</sup> and the plain, he built towers in the desert and dug many wells. <sup>ⓕ</sup> And since he was a lover of the soil, he had farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fertile lands. <sup>[6]</sup>
CSB17.11: Uzziah had an army equipped for combat that went out to war by division according to their assignments, as recorded by Jeiel the court secretary and Maaseiah the officer under the authority of Hananiah, one of the king’s commanders.
CSB17.12: The total number of family heads was 2,600 valiant warriors.
CSB17.13: Under their authority was an army of 307,500 equipped for combat, a powerful force to help the king against the enemy. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.14: Uzziah provided the entire army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and slingstones.
CSB17.15: He made skillfully designed devices in Jerusalem to shoot arrows and catapult large stones for use on the towers and on the corners. So his fame spread even to distant places, for he was wondrously helped until he became strong.
CSB17.16: But when he became strong, he grew arrogant, <sup>ⓗ</sup> and it led to his own destruction. He acted unfaithfully against the LORD his God by going into the LORD’s sanctuary to burn incense on the incense altar. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.17: The priest Azariah, <sup>ⓙ</sup> along with eighty brave priests of the LORD, went in after him.
CSB17.18: They took their stand <sup>ⓚ</sup> against King Uzziah and said, “Uzziah, you have no right to offer incense to the LORD <sup>ⓛ</sup>  — only the consecrated priests, the descendants of Aaron, have the right to offer incense. <sup>ⓜ</sup> Leave the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully! You will not receive honor from the LORD God.”
CSB17.19: Uzziah, with a firepan in his hand to offer incense, was enraged. But when he became enraged with the priests, in the presence of the priests in the LORD’s temple beside the altar of incense, a skin disease <sup>ⓝ</sup> broke out on his forehead.
CSB17.20: Then Azariah the chief priest and all the priests turned to him and saw that he was diseased on his forehead. They rushed him out of there. He himself also hurried to get out because the LORD had afflicted him.
CSB17.21: So King Uzziah was diseased to the time of his death. <sup>ⓐ</sup> He lived in quarantine <sup>[7]</sup> <sup>ⓑ</sup> with a serious skin disease and was excluded from access to the LORD’s temple, while his son Jotham was over the king’s household governing the people of the land.
CSB17.22: Now the prophet Isaiah <sup>ⓒ</sup> son of Amoz wrote about the rest of the events of Uzziah’s reign, from beginning to end.
CSB17.23: Uzziah rested with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the burial ground of the kings’ cemetery, <sup>ⓓ</sup> for they said, “He has a skin disease.” His son Jotham became king in his place.

AMP.1: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
AMP.2: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah after the king [Amaziah] slept with his fathers [in death].
AMP.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jechiliah of Jerusalem.
AMP.4: He did right in the sight of the LORD, in accordance with everything that his father Amaziah had done.
AMP.5: He continued to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding through the vision of God; and as long as he sought (inquired of, longing for) the LORD, God caused him to prosper.
AMP.6: He went out and made war against the Philistines, and broke through the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities near Ashdod and [elsewhere] among the Philistines.
AMP.7: God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.
AMP.8: The Ammonites paid tribute (money) to Uzziah, and his fame spread abroad, even as far as the border of Egypt, for he became very strong.
AMP.9: Uzziah also built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and at the corner buttress [of the wall], and fortified them.
AMP.10: He also built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns, for he had a great deal of livestock, both in the lowlands and in the plain. He also had farmers and vinedressers in the hill country and in the fertile fields, for he loved the soil.
AMP.11: Moreover, Uzziah had an army ready for battle, which went into combat by divisions according to the number of their muster as recorded by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the official, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
AMP.12: The total number of the heads of the fathers' households, of valiant men, was 2,600.
AMP.13: Under their command was an army of 307,500, who could wage war with great power, to help the king against the enemy.
AMP.14: Moreover, Uzziah prepared shields, spears, helmets, body armor, bows, and sling stones for the entire army.
AMP.15: In Jerusalem he made machines of war invented by skillful men to be put on the towers and on the [corner] battlements for the purpose of shooting arrows and large stones. And his fame spread far, for he was marvelously helped until he was strong.
AMP.16: But when Uzziah became strong, he became so proud [of himself and his accomplishments] that he acted corruptly, and he was unfaithful and sinned against the LORD his God, for he went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
AMP.17: Then Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, men of courage.
AMP.18: They opposed King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron who have been consecrated to burn incense. Get out of the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful and will have no honor from the LORD God."
AMP.19: Then Uzziah, with a censer in his hand to burn incense, was enraged; and while he was enraged with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the incense altar.
AMP.20: As Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked toward him, behold, he was leprous on his forehead; and they hurried him out of there, and he also hurried to get out because the LORD had stricken him.
AMP.21: King Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death; and, being a leper, he lived in a separate house, for he was excluded from the house of the LORD. And his son Jotham took charge of the king's household, judging and governing the people of the land.
AMP.22: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from the first to the last, Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, has written.
AMP.23: So Uzziah slept with his fathers [in death], and they buried him with his fathers in the burial field of the kings [outside the royal tombs], for they said, "He is a leper." And his son Jotham became king in his place.

MSG.1: The people of Judah then took Uzziah, who was only sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
MSG.2: The first thing he did after his father was dead and buried was to recover Elath for Judah and rebuild it.
MSG.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king and reigned for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
MSG.4: He behaved well in the eyes of God, following in the footsteps of his father Amaziah.
MSG.5: He was a loyal seeker of God. He was well trained by his pastor and teacher Zechariah to live in reverent obedience before God, and for as long as Zechariah lived, Uzziah lived a godly life. And God prospered him.
MSG.6: He ventured out and fought the Philistines, breaking into the fortress cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod. He also built settlements around Ashdod and other Philistine areas.
MSG.7: God helped him in his wars with the Philistines, the Arabs in Gur Baal, and the Meunites.
MSG.8: The Ammonites also paid tribute. Uzziah became famous, his reputation extending all the way to Egypt. He became quite powerful.
MSG.9: Uzziah constructed defense towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and at the corner of the wall.
MSG.10: He also built towers and dug cisterns out in the country. He had herds of cattle down in the foothills and out on the plains, had farmers and vinedressers at work in the hills and fields—he loved growing things.
MSG.11: On the military side, Uzziah had a well-prepared army ready to fight. They were organized by companies under the direction of Jeiel the secretary, Maaseiah the field captain, and Hananiah of the general staff.
MSG.12: The roster of family leaders over the fighting men accounted for 2,600.
MSG.13: Under them were reinforcement troops numbering 307,000, with 500 of them on constant alert—a strong royal defense against any attack.
MSG.14: Uzziah had them well-armed with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and slingshots.
MSG.15: He also installed the latest in military technology on the towers and corners of Jerusalem for shooting arrows and hurling stones. He became well known for all this—a famous king. Everything seemed to go his way.
MSG.16: But then the strength and success went to his head. Arrogant and proud, he fell. One day, contemptuous of God, he walked into The Temple of God like he owned it and took over, burning incense on the Incense Altar.
MSG.17: The priest Azariah, backed up by eighty brave priests of God, tried to prevent him.
MSG.18: They confronted Uzziah: "You must not, you cannot do this, Uzziah—only the Aaronite priests, especially consecrated for the work, are permitted to burn incense. Get out of God's Temple; you are unfaithful and a disgrace!"
MSG.19: But Uzziah, censer in hand, was already in the middle of doing it and angrily rebuffed the priests. He lost his temper; angry words were exchanged—and then, even as they quarreled, a skin disease appeared on his forehead.
MSG.20: As soon as they saw it, the chief priest Azariah and the other priests got him out of there as fast as they could. He hurried out—he knew that God then and there had given him the disease.
MSG.21: Uzziah had his skin disease for the rest of his life and had to live in quarantine; he was not permitted to set foot in The Temple of God. His son Jotham, who managed the royal palace, took over the government of the country.
MSG.22: The rest of the history of Uzziah, from start to finish, was written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
MSG.23: When Uzziah died, they buried him with his ancestors in a field next to the royal cemetery. His skin disease disqualified him from burial in the royal cemetery. His son Jotham became the next king.
